evidence: Premises hold, with a conditional trigger: DESIGN-NOTES.md:238 and CURRENT-DESIGN.md:30 permit session-start /seat; DESIGN-NOTES.md:193 allows an unbound context to propose a create/resurrect/rebind plan, so creation is possible but not inevitable. DESIGN-NOTES.md:263 explicitly identifies automatic matching/creation as conflicting with restoration into a fresh location; :265 and :273 require adopting the undo command's current pane. Full-text searches across all four artifacts for binding/rebind, resurrection, recovery/restore/undo, adoption, reuse, and retirement found no rule for a seat/clone already created in that pane before undo. Generic conflict repair at :289 and acknowledged open restoration details in CURRENT-DESIGN.md:49 do not specify disposition of its independent seat ID, channels, or history. If bootstrap has created that identity, adopting the same pane into the archived seat cannot be planned unambiguously while preserving identity/provenance (DESIGN-NOTES.md:300-302) and avoiding a leftover recovery pane (:265). This materially affects the stated closure-recovery experience; it is an acknowledged design-stage gap, with no claim of observed data loss.
